_purpose: ManualDriveController with NO physical input device. input_type=stub returns an all-zero PedalSteerCommand every frame and ffb_enabled=false keeps SDL2 out of the picture entirely, so a scenario referencing this config runs headless, in CI, and alongside other processes without touching the G29 or contending for its device index. override.enabled=false pins both domains permanently MANUAL (OverrideManager.cpp:208-214), which is what makes 'ManualDrive is writing every frame' a property of the config rather than of what a driver happened to do.

adas._note_lka: req-vd-ad:REQ-AD-027 / vd-func:FUNC-080 (phase D). adas_lka_warning_only is the LDW MODE of this same function, not a second enable: it keeps the departure judgement (and every gt.lka.* diagnostic) running and suppresses only the correction, which is what makes step f's two configurations differ in exactly one observable. Every threshold below REQUIRES CALIBRATION (verification plan section 5); LaneKeepAssistConfig's own member initializers are the C++-side single source of truth and these values mirror them.

adas_buttons._note: req-vd-ad:REQ-AD-026 step e/h, REQ-AD-030 -- physical wheel button indices for the ADAS stalk, -1 = unassigned. The headless stub has no wheel, so all six stay unassigned: verification drives them through ScriptedInputSource's `buttons` channel, which writes the ButtonBits mask directly and therefore does not go through this mapping at all. They are present here anyway because the batch harness (_write_manualdrive_config) refuses an override key that appears nowhere in this base file, and a future scenario may want to leave a note about which physical button an operation stands for.
